abilities.name: Transmutation: Denial of Darkness
abilities.description:
Transmutation: Denial of Darkness
Deal 3 consecutive instances of Pyro DMG to opponents in front, reverse Essential Transmutation, and enter the Denial of Darkness state for 30s.
_curatorNotes: The Dark commit, WIRED via the post-P4 #2 normal-opened transient state (2026-07-17): a state-gated normal ability (conditions state:transmuting) that resolveActiveAbility prefers over Radiant Wingslash while the window is open; its first swing's recovery opens `darkForm` (30s, gcsim AddStatus(blackKey, 30*60)) and consumes transmuting + whiteForm (gcsim DeleteStatus(skillWindowKey)/(whiteKey)).

Frames = gcsim skill.go skillRecastBlackFrames (InitAbilSlice(67); ActionSwap=43, ActionAttack=64, ActionSkill=48, ActionBurst=45, ActionDash=42, ActionJump=41) — gcsim attack.go Attack() routes to skillRecastBlack while skillWindowKey is active, so the commit rides the N input with the recast's own animation. 3 hits 130.0%+95.8%+116.4% ATK Pyro at T10 (skillBlack[*][9]), hitmarks 32/37/42f. Frame-represented, not an effect.

Altitude caveats: an N3 token during the window cycles this single-entry hits array for every swing (per-token ability resolution — only the first swing is the real commit; the later swings' frames are approximate). A C or P token during the window resolves this ability and finds no chargeFrames/plungeFrames (zero-width block / dropped plunge) — the window is 6s, so this is a degenerate notation, not a rotation-relevant path.

[A7] Caveat removed. Follow-up N presses within one token during the window cycle the single-entry hits array, so only the first swing is the real commit and later swings are approximate — a degenerate, non-rotation-relevant path (already in this ability's curator notes).

↻ 2026-09-04 (⚓ Nate): infusion 'pyro'. THE DARK COMMIT IS NOT A NORMAL ATTACK — gcsim attack.go:46 routes the attack button straight to skillRecastBlack() while skillWindowKey is active, and that builds an AttackInfo tagged AttackTagElementalArt / ICDTagElementalArt with Element Pyro and Durability 25. It rides the N input and this ability's frames are already the recast's own, but its ELEMENT was still resolving as an ordinary physical claymore swing, so the commit applied nothing to the gauge. ⚓ `infusion` is the right field for the same reason a stance's is: the WINDOW is the ability's own gate, so nothing has to be tracked — `resolveActiveAbility` only picks this ability while `transmuting` is live, and the commit closes that window via actionOpensState.consumes.

⚠️ ONE application, and it agrees with gcsim for two independent reasons. gcsim throws THREE hits (skillBlackHitmarks {32, 37, 42}) on ICDGroupDurinSkill — an 18f window with sequence {1,0,0} — so only the first of the three applies; and our per-swing model is one hit per swing anyway (the documented approximation). ⚠️ Our swing walks Durin's NORMAL ICD counter rather than an elemental-art one, which is inert here: every other Durin normal is PHYSICAL and a physical swing reaches no clock at all, so this commit is the counter's only user. ⛔ Don't reach for a per-ability ICD tag on that account.

⛔ No `hit` frame authored though gcsim's first hitmark is 32. The FrameMap already states every key frameAt() can ask for (N/E/Q/D/J/swap), so `hit` would only ever be a fallback for a key that is present — inert — and the field's meaning is the hitmark of an InitNormalCancelSlice, whose E/Q/D/J/swap entries EQUAL it. This slice is an InitAbilSlice and they do not (48/45/42/41/43 against a hitmark of 32), so authoring it would state something untrue to buy nothing.

abilities.name: Binary Form: Convergence and Division

_curatorNotes: Energy restored to Durin when he enters a form (Confirmation of Purity / Denial of Darkness) via the Skill recast — 33 at talent level 10 (gcsim skill.go skillEnergy[T10]=33), once per 6s (energyIcdKey=6*60). In-game it fires on the COMMIT, not this tap; kept on the tap because the Dark commit is a normal-attack action and effects don't dispatch from normals (post-P4 #2 substrate-only decision) — placing it on the White commit alone would be asymmetric. Timing error ≤ the 6s window and the 6s ICD absorbs it.

↻ 2026-08-18: the REASON above is stale, the PLACEMENT is not. "effects don't dispatch from normals (post-P4 #2 substrate-only decision)" is no longer true as written — `onHit` effects DO dispatch per-swing from normals (`dispatchHit` at sim/run.ts:327/1145, plus the N/CA/P onHit pools in buffWindows.ts:624+). Two reasons that outlive it keep this effect on the tap: (1) `handleCast` is reached only by a skill/burst TOKEN (run.ts:998-1000), so an `onCast` trigger can never fire from the Dark commit, which is a normal ACTION — the asymmetry argument stands unchanged; (2) an `energy` effect has NO planner consumer at all — the only reader in src is `deriveCapabilities` (deriveCapabilities.ts:300), and its Energy facet excludes `target: 'self'` (:628), so nothing renders wherever it is placed. ⏭ Move it to the two commits if a primitive for "a normal-action cast grants energy" ever lands; until then the 6s-window timing approximation costs nothing visible.

abilities.description:
Purify the substance of souls and wishes to undergo **Essential Transmutation**. While transmuted, Durin's Elemental Skill Binary Form: Convergence and Division will be replaced with the special Elemental Skill Transmutation: Confirmation of Purity, and the Normal Attack Radiant Wingslash will be replaced with the special Elemental Skill Transmutation: Denial of Darkness.

Transmutation: Confirmation of Purity
Deal 1 instance of AoE Pyro DMG to nearby opponents, reverse Essential Transmutation, and enter the Confirmation of Purity state for 30s.

Transmutation: Denial of Darkness
Deal 3 consecutive instances of Pyro DMG to opponents in front, reverse Essential Transmutation, and enter the Denial of Darkness state for 30s.

When Durin enters the Confirmation of Purity or Denial of Darkness state while in battle, he will restore a certain amount of Elemental Energy. Elemental Energy can be restored this way once every 6s.
_curatorNotes: Base frames = the opening tap E that enters Essential Transmutation (gcsim skill.go skillFrames, InitAbilSlice(49); ActionSwap=13, ActionAttack=16, ActionSkill=15, ActionBurst=4, ActionDash=14, ActionJump=14). The tap deals no damage and sets the 12s CD (SetCD(action.ActionSkill, 12*60)); the commits do not re-set CD (separate abilities with their own timing). CD/energy verified against the talent sidecar.

DUAL-FORM MODEL — WIRED 2026-07-17 (post-P4 #2, the 'normal-attack opens a mode state' primitive; Nate 2026-07-15 chose faithful auto-tracking over a user-assertion workaround). (1) This tap opens `transmuting` (6s, gcsim skillWindowDur) via opensTransientState — behavior is `instant`, not stance: the tap itself has no lasting on-field mode. (2) WHITE commit = durin__skill__transmutation_confirmation_of_purity, a separate skill gated state:transmuting (Flins Northland-Spearstorm pattern). (3) DARK commit = durin__normal__transmutation_denial_of_darkness, a state-gated normal whose actionOpensState.normal opens `darkForm` — the post-P4 #2 primitive. (4) BURST reads the form: base Q = White (default); durin__burst__principle_of_darkness_as_the_stars_smolder is gated state:darkForm and carries the Dragon of Dark Decay. Both commits `consumes` the window + the opposite form (gcsim DeleteStatus pairs). The former input-less placeholder variants are deleted; their frames live on the new abilities.
[A7] Compression drops: the 6s Essential Transmutation window duration; White commit = single AoE Pyro hit, Dark commit = 3 front Pyro hits (both frame-represented, in curator notes).

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — The 30s darkForm/whiteForm window draws NO bar anywhere — `openTransientState` pushes a state window record and no timeline projection renders state windows (grep of src/lib/timeline finds no 'state' lane). The player commits a form, sees an ordinary N block, and the 30s window that decides the next Q bar's identity is a blank. The trim drops the (support)/(damage) role gloss, which is kit trivia. Category: expected-but-absent.
nonHitting (non-hitting casts round, 2026-09-16 (docs/nonhitting-casts-round.md §1)): gcsim durin/skill.go:59-73 — the tap opens the transmuting window and sets the CD; only the two commits attack.

abilities.name: Transmutation: Confirmation of Purity
abilities.description:
Transmutation: Confirmation of Purity
Deal 1 instance of AoE Pyro DMG to nearby opponents, reverse Essential Transmutation, and enter the Confirmation of Purity state for 30s.
_curatorNotes: The White commit, reachable via a second E during `transmuting` (resolveActiveAbility prefers this conditioned skill; separate ability id → separate charge queue, so the base 12s clock is untouched — gcsim: recast sets no CD and ActionReady bypasses the CD check while the window is active). cooldown: 0 mirrors that.

Frames = gcsim skill.go skillRecastWhiteFrames (InitAbilSlice(83); ActionSwap=48, ActionAttack=62, ActionSkill=53, ActionBurst=50, ActionDash=46, ActionJump=47). Deals 190.1% ATK Pyro at T10 (skillWhite[9]=1.9008), hitmark 35f — frame-represented, not authored as an effect.

opensTransientState opens `whiteForm` (30s, gcsim AddStatus(whiteKey, 30*60)) and consumes transmuting + darkForm (gcsim DeleteStatus(skillWindowKey)/(blackKey)). whiteForm gates nothing directly (the White burst is the unconditioned default) but is tracked for gcsim fidelity and so the Dark commit's `consumes` displacement is visible on the timeline.

[A7] Caveat removed as working behavior: the recast is a separate ability (cooldown 0, own charge queue) so the base 12s CD, set by the first press, is shown ticking through the recast — correctly modeled, no divergence.

application[] AUTHORED 2026-09-16 (T0.5). gcsim skillRecastWhite (skill.go:75-90) queues 190.1% ATK Pyro with Durability 25 at skillWhiteHitmarks = 35. The field was absent, so the parse fell back to the character's element AT THE CAST and flagged it provisional — measured 'Durin E E Q' drew 0.25pyro? , 35 frames early and wearing the --ui-provisional foot. ⚠️ The oracle cannot reach this cast (the dumper panics on 'unexpected charges less than 0'), so the number is a source read — the same way the sibling Dark burst's were derived.

abilities.name: Principle of Purity: As the Light Shifts

_curatorNotes: Dragon of White Flame periodic AoE Pyro tick, 170.4% ATK at T10 (gcsim burst.go burstWhiteDoT[9]=1.70352). 20 ticks, interval 58.8f = 0.98s (burstTicksWhite=20, burstIntervalWhite=58.8). Follows the active character. A4 Primordial Fusion amp (up to +75% on the first 10 ticks, +3% per 100 ATK) is NOT baked in — dynamic ATK-scaling, per-tick consumption.

icdGate authored 2026-08-17 (ICD-group round b): gcsim burst.go:120 sets ICDGroupDurinBurstWhite on this tick, whose table entry is a 90f reset window in which only the FIRST hit applies. Measured 7/13 applied against standard ICD's 6. ⚠️ The Dark Decay counterpart is deliberately NOT authored — gcsim gives it ICDGroupDurinBurstBlack (120f, first only), but the oracle has no capture of the dark form (the driver cannot reach it), and an unmeasured pair is a claim rather than data.

↻ 2026-09-04 (stale-application[] pass, tier 2): firstTickDelay 0.983 authored EXPLICITLY. ⚠️ It was absent, and absent does NOT mean zero — `summonTickSeries` defaults firstDelay to the INTERVAL (summons.ts:296), which put the first tick at 97 + 58.8 = 155.8 against gcsim's 156. So this is a no-op numerically and is authored for exactness and for symmetry with the Dark series, where the same default was 5 frames early. gcsim burst.go: burstFirstTickDelayWhite = 154 + 60 - 58.8 = 155.2, first task at ceil() = 156 from the cast; the summon spawns at 97 (burstInitHitmark[0]), so 59f = 0.983s from spawn.

⛔ NO tickCap, and that is checked rather than assumed: gcsim fires burstTicksWhite = 20, and our window (spawnsAt 97 + 20s) with this firstTickDelay and interval yields exactly 20. The tick-cap round's rule is that absent is right unless the count diverges from duration ÷ interval, and here it does not.

abilities.description:
Unleash the power of the "Beast" in different ways. Durin can use different Elemental Bursts based on his **Essential Transmutation** state.

Principle of Purity: As the Light Shifts
When Durin is in the Confirmation of Purity state, he will use the Elemental Burst Principle of Purity: As the Light Shifts, dealing 3 instances of AoE Pyro DMG to opponents in front, and manifesting his power in the Dragon of White Flame form. The Dragon of White Flame will follow the current active character and attack nearby opponents at intervals, dealing AoE Pyro DMG. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG.

Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder
When Durin is in the Denial of Darkness state, he will use the Elemental Burst Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder, dealing 3 instances of AoE Pyro DMG to opponents in front, and manifesting his power in the Dragon of Dark Decay form. The Dragon of Dark Decay will follow the current active character and periodically attack a single nearby opponent, dealing Pyro DMG. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG.

When Durin is not in a special state as a result of Essential Transmutation, he will use the Elemental Burst Principle of Purity: As the Light Shifts.
_curatorNotes: Burst frames from gcsim burst.go burstFrames (InitAbilSlice(104); ActionSwap=102, ActionAttack=103, ActionSkill=103, ActionDash=102, ActionJump=104, ActionWalk=102). SetCD(action.ActionBurst, 18*60) = 18s, no delay; EnergyMax 70 — both verified vs sidecar. White opening 3 hits at T10: 214.1%+173.5%+201.3% ATK Pyro (burstWhiteInitial[*][9]), hitmarks 97/121/154f; frame-represented, not effects. Summon spawnsAt=97 = burstInitHitmark[0] (where the dragon manifests; gcsim burstDuration starts here, internally 20.5s vs the 20s field lifetime shown). Corrected stub behavior from 'stance' to 'instant' + summons: the Burst is an instant cast that spawns a following dragon — the form state lives on the Skill, not here. C4 +40% Burst DMG, C6 30%/70% DEF-ignore, and C1 Cycle-of-Enlightenment flat-DMG are noted on their constellation entries.

Dark form split out 2026-07-17 (post-P4 #2): the former input-less Dark variant is now durin__burst__principle_of_darkness_as_the_stars_smolder, gated state:darkForm — resolveActiveAbility picks it only while darkForm is live, so Q immediately, or after the 30s form expires, correctly renders White. Both bursts share the single per-character burst cooldown scalar (matching gcsim's one burst slot).
[A7] Caveat removed as working behavior: default-form selection and the following-dragon ticks (~0.98s, 20s) are shown; the un-modeled A4 dragon amp is noted on the Chaos Formed passive instead.

abilities.name: Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder
abilities.description:
Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder
When Durin is in the Denial of Darkness state, he will use the Elemental Burst Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder, dealing 3 instances of AoE Pyro DMG to opponents in front, and manifesting his power in the Dragon of Dark Decay form. The Dragon of Dark Decay will follow the current active character and periodically attack a single nearby opponent, dealing Pyro DMG. This DMG is considered Elemental Burst DMG.

_curatorNotes: Dragon of Dark Decay periodic single-target Pyro tick, 233.7% ATK at T10 (gcsim burst.go burstBlackDoT[9]=2.33712). 16 ticks, interval 73.6f = 1.227s (burstTicksBlack=16, burstIntervalBlack=73.6). Follows the active character, targets one opponent. A4 Primordial Fusion amp not baked in (see the White tick note on the base Burst).

icdGate {timer: 120} authored: gcsim ICDGroupDurinBurstBlack (icd_groups.dm.go:95) is a 2s window with sequence {1,0} — only the first hit in the window applies. It was ABSENT, i.e. the standard 2.5s/every-third, which is a different rule. ⚠️ The White series has carried its own {timer: 90} all along; the two forms are on DIFFERENT ICD groups, which is why the gate belongs on the series and not on the character. ⚠️⚠️ The ICD-group round (2026-08-18) authored the WHITE series' gate and missed this one, and the reason is the same blind spot that let the white tick stream into this ability's application[]: the dumper runs one ability at C0 in an empty core and cannot reach a state-gated form, so drivers.json gives durin `darkForm: []` and it 'gets no row'. ⚓ A form the oracle cannot reach is where to look when a per-series field is missing on one half of a pair.

↻ 2026-09-04 (stale-application[] pass, tier 2): firstTickDelay 1.317 authored, and here it is a REAL correction. ⚠️ Absent does not mean zero — the default is the INTERVAL (summons.ts:296), which put the first tick at 97 + 73.8 = 170.8 against gcsim's 176: five frames early, and every one of the 16 ticks inherited it. gcsim burst.go: burstFirstTickDelayBlack = 154 + 95 - 73.6 = 175.4, first task at ceil() = 176 from the cast, so 79f = 1.317s from the summon's spawn at 97. Interval sharpened 1.23 → 1.227: burstIntervalBlack is 73.6f = 1.2267s and 1.23 was 73.8f, a 0.2f drift per tick.

⛔ NO tickCap, and that is checked rather than assumed: gcsim fires burstTicksBlack = 16, and our window (spawnsAt 97 + 20s) with this firstTickDelay and interval yields exactly 16. The tick-cap round's rule is that absent is right unless the count diverges from duration ÷ interval, and here it does not.

Split out of the base Burst's input-less variant 2026-07-17 (post-P4 #2) per the deferred design: gated state:darkForm so resolveActiveAbility auto-selects it only while the Dark form is live. Opening 3 hits at T10: 225.8%+183.2%+201.3% ATK Pyro (burstBlackInitial[*][9]); frame-represented via the shared burstFrames slice (gcsim burst.go uses one for both forms). Shares the single burst CD scalar + 70 energy cost with the White form.

[A7] Caveat removed: auto-selection while darkForm is live is working behavior and the ~1.23s cadence (16 ticks) is shown; single-target-vs-AoE and 'harder-hitting' are out of scope (the tool shows no damage numbers and does not distinguish target counts).

↻ 2026-09-04 (stale-application[] pass, tier 2): application[] trimmed from [97, 121, 154, 156, 214, 273, 332, 391, 450, 508, 567, 626, 685, 744, 802, 861] to the three OPENING hits. ⚓⚓ The head [97, 121, 154] is CORRECT and is NOT a mis-capture — gcsim burst.go:17 `burstInitHitmark = {97, 97+24, 154}` is ONE slice shared by both forms, so White and Dark genuinely land their three opening hits on the same frames and only their multipliers differ. What was wrong is the TAIL: it starts at 156 = ceil(burstFirstTickDelayWhite 155.2) and steps 58.8f, which is `burstIntervalWhite` — the WHITE dragon's tick stream, on the DARK ability, whose own series correctly runs at 73.6f. So the Dark burst was applying Pyro twice AND at the wrong cadence. ⚓ The White burst's array was already right (its three hits, no tail) and is the shape copied here. ⚠️ The dumper cannot reach this form: scripts/gcsim-dump/drivers.json gives durin `darkForm: []` and notes it 'gets no row', so these numbers are DERIVED from gcsim source, not captured — ⛔ don't 'verify' them by re-running the dumper, which will report nothing.

passives.name: Light Manifest of the Divine Calculus
passives.caveat: The RES shred is shown in either form, but in game it applies in the White form only.
_curatorNotes: gcsim asc.go a1Init: gated on c.StatusIsActive(burstKeyWhite) (Dragon of White Flame active), modeled here as state:duringSummon. Fires on team Overloaded / Burning / Pyro-Swirl / Pyro-Crystallize reactions (a1ReactToElements) shredding Pyro RES + the partner element's RES by 20% for 6s. A separate onEnemyDamage hook also shreds Pyro + Dendro RES when a Burning opponent takes Pyro or Dendro DMG — not authored as an onHit effect (the Burning-reaction path above covers the common case). Hexerei bonus: hexereiA1Bonus()=1.75 with GetHexereiCount()>=2, i.e. -35% instead of -20% — faction-count dependent, not modeled. Dark form (a1OnBurst isWhite=false) adds a ReactBonusMod of +40% to Durin's Amped (Vaporize/Melt) hits — no vaporize/melt DMG-bonus stat primitive, so unmodeled.

[A7] Base shred is authored per reaction (Pyro plus electro/anemo/geo/dendro partner element, -20%, 6s refresh) and is shown; only the 35% Hexerei-count upgrade and the Dark-form +40% Vaporize/Melt are omissions.

[Hexerei 2026-08-15] RE-AUTHORED. The five faction shreds were -15 ADDITIVE on top of the five base -20 (base + faction = the in-game -35), which was correct arithmetic and unrenderable: once factionBonuses reach the planner (docs/faction-bonuses-round.md) that draws TEN debuff bars where a reader expects five. The faction five now carry the FULL -35 and the base five are gated `not(teamFaction hexerei >=2)`, so exactly one bar per element renders in either world — -20% solo, -35% in a Hexerei team. ⛔ The alternative, teaching the projection to SUM co-located shreds, was measured and rejected: eight characters have same-element shred pairs and they are overwhelmingly ALTERNATIVES, not addends (Faruzan's two -30% Anemo entries are one shred under two condition branches, and summing them shows -60%; Venti's Breeze -12% and Storm of Defiance -20% genuinely stack but must stay separate, because provenance is the point). Durin was the only true addend pair in the corpus, and only because his -15% modified his own shred. [Hexerei 2026-07-29] Secret Rite authored in top-level factionBonuses. gcsim asc.go:138-148 hexereiA1Bonus() returns 1.75 only when IsHexerei AND Core.Player.GetHexereiCount() >= 2 — count-gated, so every A1 value is x1.75 (asc.go:58,64,82,105): res shred -0.20 -> -0.35, Dark-form Amped ReactBonusMod 0.40 -> 0.70. Authored as five ADDITIVE resShred effects of -15 (mirroring the five A1 base effects, same triggers, same duringSummon gate wrapped in an `all` with teamFaction hexerei min 2), so base -20 + faction -15 = the in-game -35; durations unchanged at 6s per the article ('all effects +75% except duration'). The Dark-form 40->70% Vaporize/Melt uplift is a self reaction-DMG multiplier with no stat primitive — caveat only, no effect. No bare IsHexerei permanent patches exist for Durin: durin.go:29-34 only reads the hexerei param (default enabled) and asc.go:139 is the sole consumer, always paired with the count check.

↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "The RES shred is shown in either form, but in game it applies in the White form only. Not modeled: the Dark form's +40% Vaporize and Melt DMG (70% with 2 or more Hexerei on the team)."
passives.description:
Durin will trigger different buffs depending on the form that his power manifests as when he unleashes his Elemental Burst. When that form is:

Dragon of White Flame
After nearby party members trigger Burning, Overloaded, Pyro Swirl, or Pyro Crystallize reactions on an opponent, or deal Pyro DMG or Dendro DMG to an opponent affected by Burning, that opponent's Pyro RES, and the RES for the corresponding Element involved in the reaction, are decreased by 20% for 6s.

Dragon of Dark Decay
Durin's Vaporize DMG is increased by 40% and his Melt DMG is increased by 40%.

passives.name: Chaos Formed Like the Night
_curatorNotes: gcsim asc.go a4OnBurst/a4Dmg: on Burst, 10 Primordial Fusion stacks for 20s; each Dragon of White Flame / Dark Decay tick consumes 1 stack for +min(TotalAtk/100*0.03, 0.75) multiplicative DMG. Dynamic ATK-scaling amp on autonomous summon ticks with a per-tick consumption budget — no clean primitive; left out of the summonTick scaling. Replaced the mismodeled genshin-db stub effect (damage scaling:3 stat:atk manual), which misrepresented an ATK-scaling self-amp as a 3%-ATK damage instance.

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — It says the amp is "not folded into the tick values shown" — there are no tick values on screen. A summon-lane tick mark says the tick HAPPENED; the tool renders no damage magnitudes at all (tool constitution). The passive authors no effects, so no bar is missing either. This is a pure DMG% omission dressed as a rendering divergence. Category: invisible-omission.
passives.description:
After unleashing an Elemental Burst, Durin gains the Primordial Fusion of Forms effect for 20s: Durin gains 10 stacks of Primordial Fusion. When a periodic attack from Dragon of White Flame or Dragon of Dark Decay deals DMG, 1 stack of Primordial Fusion will be consumed to increase the DMG dealt by 3% of the original DMG for every 100 ATK. A maximum of 75% additional DMG can be dealt this way. When a single attack from Dragon of White Flame or Dragon of Dark Decay hits multiple opponents, only one stack of Primordial Fusion is consumed.
Primordial Fusion stacks are reset when the Elemental Burst is unleashed again.

constellations.name: Adamah's Redemption
_curatorNotes: gcsim cons.go c1Init/c1OnBurst: White → teammates each get 20 Cycle stacks (Tag c1Key=20); their N/C/P/E/Q hits (while Dragon of White Flame active + they are the active char) consume 1 stack for FlatDmg += 0.6*Durin.TotalAtk. Dark → Durin gets 20 stacks; his Burst hits consume 2 for FlatDmg += 1.5*Durin.TotalAtk. Source-ATK-scaled flat DMG added onto the recipient's hits across all attack classes — no matching all-attack FlatDmg buff stat, so unmodeled. Removed the two mismodeled genshin-db stub 'damage' effects (scaling 60/150 atk manual).
[A7] Compression drops the 20s stack lifetime and the per-hit consumption counts (White 1/hit, Dark 2/Burst-hit, refreshed on Burst) — kit detail, in curator notes.

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — The blank on the buff lane. C1 is a named, 20s, Burst-granted team buff, and flat-DMG buffs ARE a shape we render as bars elsewhere (Cyno's own A4 draws normalFlatDmg/skillFlatDmg) — the gap here is only a missing all-attack-class FlatDmg Stat key, not the no-damage-numbers rule. So a C1 player casts Q, looks at the team buff rows, and correctly expects a 20s bar that never appears. The trim drops the 60%/150% magnitudes, which are the half we would never print. Category: expected-but-absent.
constellations.description:
After casting his Elemental Burst, Durin's effects will vary depending on the form of his Elemental Burst:
· Principle of Purity: As the Light Shifts: All other nearby party members gain 20 stacks of Cycle of Enlightenment lasting 20s. When nearby active characters deal Normal Attack, Charged Attack, Plunging Attack, Elemental Skill, or Elemental Burst DMG, 1 stack of Cycle of Enlightenment will be consumed to increase the DMG dealt by 60% of Durin's ATK. Stack counts for characters in the party who have Cycle of Enlightenment are managed individually.
· Principle of Darkness: As the Stars Smolder: Durin gains 20 stacks of Cycle of Enlightenment lasting 20s. When Durin deals Elemental Burst DMG, 2 stacks of Cycle of Enlightenment will be consumed to increase the DMG dealt by 150% of Durin's ATK.
